who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code, dst-1113
where: blaze-vm:/root/loop.sh and the smoke before a merge (how-to H-smoke-before-merge)
what: The smoke of a branch built through `/root/loop.sh` fails at its first step: `hello cold FAILED: exited 101`, `error: linking .../out/hello: ... is a launched run (`blaze run`), and blaze`s launcher /root/inst/<branch>/blaze-launcher does not read: No such file or directory`. loop.sh builds `-p blaze-thin -p blaze-engine` and installs those two; `blaze run` on main needs `blaze-launcher` beside them. The how-to`s command also calls `blaze run -q -p scripts --bin smoke`, and the VM has no `blaze` on its PATH (exit 127).
cost: three smoke runs (one killed by a dropped ix session, one exit 127, one a real FAILED quote) before the first that could pass
cause: the launcher became a separate binary after loop.sh was written, and the how-to assumes a released blaze the VM does not have
class: a shared build script that installs less than the program now needs, so every lane`s first smoke fails the same way
prevention: loop.sh builds and installs blaze-launcher, and the how-to builds the smoke program with cargo on the VM; not done: the script is shared, so I worked around it in my own job
workaround: inside the loop.sh call: `cargo build --release -p blaze-launcher`, copy it beside $BLAZE, `cargo build -q -p scripts --bin smoke`, run target/debug/smoke; all as a systemd unit, since an ix session can drop
